quotes.text: It automatically determines the available plans and conditions, generates a localized description, and displays it in your form’s theme.
platforms that create direct charges must identify the connected account that renders the Payment Method Messaging Element.

If you use [Dynamic payment methods](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods/dynamic-payment-methods.md), the Payment Method Messaging Element automatically pulls your payment method preferences from the [Stripe Dashboard](https://dashboard.stripe.com/settings/payment_methods)

Messaging doesn’t render if the [countryCode](https://docs.stripe.com/js/elements_object/create_element?type=paymentMethodMessaging#elements_create-options-countryCode) and [currency](https://docs.stripe.com/js/elements_object/create_element?type=paymentMethodMessaging#elements_create-options-currency) combination passed has no eligible payment plans.
You’re responsible for compliance with applicable laws, rules, and regulations regarding the promotion of buy now, pay later payment options.

findings: Both same-URL captures describe the web Payment Method Messaging Element as localized BNPL plan messaging for product, cart, and payment pages. The rendered plans depend on customer location, currency, and amount; only pay-now options or a countryCode/currency combination without eligible plans produce no message (new raw:7-9,93-101,169; old raw:6-8,98-106,180). The page describes messaging, not payment authorization or a completed financing application.

Both captures show plain Stripe.js and React Stripe.js mounting with a publishable key, amount, currency, and optional countryCode in examples (new raw:17-79; old raw:16-84). The changed script path from js.stripe.com/dahlia/stripe.js to js.stripe.com/endive/stripe.js is a versioned example-path change (diff:7-12), not evidence of a new runtime rule or migration requirement.

For Connect direct charges, the platform must identify the connected account rendering the element by setting stripeAccount on the Stripe instance before element creation (new raw:83-91; old raw:88-96). Dynamic payment methods pull Dashboard preferences only if that feature is used; manual paymentMethodTypes remains an alternative and eligibility filtering still applies. Default dynamic ordering can be changed with paymentMethodOrder (new raw:99-146; old raw:104-157).

The info modal still shows a usage overview, per-plan terms summary, and full-terms links; Affirm, Afterpay/Clearpay, and Klarna remain listed, with Klarna limited here to one-time payments (new raw:148-169; old raw:159-180). Appearance options and merchant responsibility for data-use disclosures and BNPL-promotion compliance also persist (new raw:171-208; old raw:182-222).

The diff changes sample JavaScript formatting, list numbering, heading whitespace, the sample Stripe.js release path, an image URL, and an Afterpay/Clearpay documentation anchor; no changed plan eligibility, provider list, Connect account identity, or compliance obligation appears in the two captures (diff:1-241). The changed release path and hyperlinks should be retained as dated navigation/examples, not inferred deprecation of older integrations.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Preserve the 2026-04-21 source as a dated capture of web messaging behavior, supported BNPL names, eligibility and no-render conditions, Connect direct-charge account identity, information modal, and legal responsibilities (old raw:8-220; new raw:9-206).

Preserve Klarna's one-time-payment limitation (old raw:178; new raw:167), Dashboard preference loading conditional on use of Dynamic payment methods (old raw:106; new raw:101), and the fact that manual method selection still undergoes eligibility filtering.

Preserve both captured Stripe.js script paths as dated examples (old raw:19; new raw:20); the new path alone does not establish whether the old path is unsupported or whether a deployment must switch.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/elements/payment-method-messaging, the November capture still describes a web BNPL messaging component that determines eligible plans from amount, currency, and customer location, with no rendering where no eligible plan exists (new raw:9,93-101,169; old raw:8,98-106,180). [[source-stripe-payment-method-messaging-element]] covers the three named providers and Connect direct-charge account setting. Dashboard preferences are pulled if Dynamic payment methods are used; manual paymentMethodTypes remains an alternative, subject to eligibility filtering (new raw:101; old raw:106). This does not itself perform payment authorization.
answers.Q2: The same-URL comparison at https://docs.stripe.com/elements/payment-method-messaging shows no substantive BNPL messaging or eligibility rule change; diff:1-241 mainly changes example formatting, the versioned Stripe.js script path, and documentation or image links (old raw:19,162,177; new raw:20,151,166). However, [[source-stripe-payment-method-messaging-element]]:19,46 and its concept:34 need a bounded pre-existing claim correction: both captures make Dashboard preference loading conditional on using Dynamic payment methods (old raw:106; new raw:101), while default dynamic ordering is a separate rule (old raw:157; new raw:146).
